text: The authors state that for recursive reward modeling to scale, agent A(k-1)'s task must be simpler and in a narrower domain than A(k)'s; if Assumption 2 holds, the recursion builds a hierarchy of increasingly capable agents. They describe recursive reward modeling as an instance of iterated amplification using reward modeling instead of supervised or imitation learning.
title: Recursion scales only if assisting tasks are simpler; RRM as an instance of amplification
